home.heritageTitle: A celebration of family and roots

ourStory.heading: Our Story
ourStory.howWeMetBody: [John and Diana's story will be added here.]
ourStory.heritageBody: Imanalla, welcome. Diana's roots are in Otavalo, an Andean community known for its Kichwa language, music, and extraordinary weaving traditions. Otavalo textiles carry generations of artistry, patience, and identity, while Andean values honor family, reciprocity, and Pachamama—Mother Earth. As John and Diana begin married life, they carry those roots with gratitude. This celebration also honors kuyay, the Kichwa word for love: love of family, love of place, and the love that brings all of us together in Quito.

itinerary.heading: Suggested Itinerary
itinerary.intro: This is a suggested itinerary for guests who would like to explore Quito before the wedding. Please adapt it to your arrival date, energy level, mobility, and interests—rest is part of the plan, especially at altitude.
itinerary.altitudeAdvisory: Altitude advisory: take it easy, hydrate, and avoid heavy meals or alcohol while acclimating.
itinerary.alternateArrivalsIntro: Arriving later in the week? These shorter options keep the pace gentle so you can enjoy the wedding day.
itinerary.timeZoneNote: All times below are Ecuador time (ECT, UTC−5). Ecuador does not observe daylight saving time.

travel.heading: Travel
travel.airportInfoBody: Fly into Mariscal Sucre International Airport (UIO), about 45–60 minutes from Old Town depending on traffic. Official airport taxis are typically about $26 to central Quito, and the airport express bus is about $8.
travel.altitudeTip: Quito sits at about 9,350 feet / 2,850 meters. Plan a gentle first day, drink water, and give yourself time to acclimate.
travel.weatherTip: March is part of the wet season. Expect cool mornings and evenings, possible rain, strong high-altitude sun, and temperatures around 50–69°F. Pack layers and a light rain jacket.
travel.currencyTip: Ecuador uses the U.S. Dollar. Small bills are helpful for taxis, markets, and tips.
travel.safetyTip: Use official taxis or trusted ride-share options, keep valuables close in busy areas, and take normal big-city precautions in Old Town.
travel.stayIntro: A few 4★ and 5★ hotels in Quito's Old Town, within easy walking distance of the Basílica and Hotel Plaza Grande. Estimated rates are approximate; please verify for March 2027.
travel.sightseeingIntro: If you are extending your trip, here are some of the most memorable things to see in and around Quito.

sightseeing.name: Old Town walking tour
sightseeing.details: Plaza Grande, La Compañía (gold-leaf interior), San Francisco, and Calle La Ronda — all walkable from the Plaza.

sightseeing.name: TelefériQo cable car
sightseeing.details: Cable car climbs to about 3,945 m for sweeping city and Andes views; round-trip about $8.50. Go early before clouds.

sightseeing.name: Mitad del Mundo
sightseeing.details: Equator monument about 45 minutes north of Quito; entry around $5. Combine with Museo Solar Inti Ñan for fun gravity demonstrations.

sightseeing.name: Mindo Cloud Forest
sightseeing.details: Birding and waterfalls about 2 hours northwest. 450+ species recorded — a local guide makes the morning unforgettable.

sightseeing.name: Otavalo Market (Saturday)
sightseeing.details: Famous Andean textile market about 2 hours north — best experienced on a Saturday morning.

sightseeing.name: Galápagos · Cuenca · Amazon
sightseeing.details: Multi-day add-ons. Galápagos and Cuenca need domestic flights; the Amazon is reached via Coca. Build in extra time and check vaccine guidance for the jungle.

travel.healthBody: No special vaccines are required for Quito itself. Yellow fever vaccine is recommended if extending to the Amazon and required by some countries on re-entry. Drink bottled or filtered water (hotels usually provide it), pack SPF 30+ and a hat for the intense high-altitude sun, and give your body 24–48 hours to acclimate before strenuous activities. Pharmacies ("farmacias") are common throughout Quito for over-the-counter needs.
travel.connectivityIntro: Several easy options for data and calls while you're in Ecuador.

connectivity.name: US carrier roaming
connectivity.details: T-Mobile, Verizon, and AT&T plans typically include Ecuador data, though speeds may be slower than at home. Verify your plan before flying.

connectivity.name: eSIM (recommended)
connectivity.details: Airalo and Holafly sell Ecuador eSIMs from about $5–15 for 1–2 GB. Install before flying and activate on arrival — no SIM swap needed.

connectivity.name: Local SIM
connectivity.details: Claro and Movistar sell prepaid SIMs at UIO airport for around $10 with a few GB of data. Bring an unlocked phone.

connectivity.name: WiFi
connectivity.details: Most hotels, cafés, and restaurants in Quito offer free WiFi to customers.
